evidence: Plaut. Rud. 4.7.9: ubi dēcipiuntur dolīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to catch, as in a snare (dēcipula, a trap).

evidence: Traupman 312: fall for a trick, fallī
terms.comment: The wider word: besides deceiving it means to escape someone’s notice and to let them down (nisi mē fallit animus, Cic.; spēs fefellit).

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Traupman p. 102: verba tibi iste dat
terms.comment: “Give someone (mere) words”: to fool them, never to give one’s word (see word).

phrases.latin: tunc dēmum ingemuit corvī dēceptus stupor
phrases.english: only then did the foolish crow, tricked, groan

phrases.latin: nunc referam grātiam atque eās itidem fallam, ut ab īs fallimur?
phrases.english: shall I now pay them back and trick them just as we’re tricked by them?
a man who is hard to fool
